discovery: Discovery of metal-halide perovskites as highly efficient photovoltaic and optoelectronic semiconductors
subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics (semiconductor optoelectronics)
motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka first used organolead halide perovskites as light absorbers in solar cells. In 2012 Park and Snaith independently showed that solid-state perovskite devices work efficiently, and Snaith found that the perovskite itself carries charge over long distances. These discoveries created a new class of semiconductor. Solution-processed, defect-tolerant materials made at low temperature reach sharp band edges, long carrier diffusion lengths and single-junction efficiencies above 26 percent, rivalling crystalline silicon within about fifteen years. This goes against the accepted belief that high-performance semiconductors must be ultra-pure and grown at high temperature. It has opened new physics: benign defect states, polaronic screening, ion migration and hot-carrier dynamics. It has also produced perovskite-silicon tandems, LEDs and detectors now entering industry. The discovery came from chemical intuition about materials, and it has changed the physics and technology of semiconductors.
